Improve the ability of the USG, host countries and other partners to prepare for and mitigate the effects of disasters, including both natural disasters and complex emergencies, taking into account the differences in men and womens freedom of movement and access to information. Activities under this component include any efforts to enhance the capacities of the USG (in Washington and in the field), humanitarian assistance providers, national host-country authorities, and local communities to engage in disaster reduction and response activities. Activities consist of standardized and coordinated assessments, monitoring, information sharing, data and situational analysis, joint planning; enhancement of coping mechanisms, including the capacity to address adaptation to constantly changing situations on the ground including climate variability and climate change.

Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Enhancing the Quality, Utility, and Access to Low-cost (EQUAL) Compute Network

description.narrative: IDRC launched Enhancing the Quality, Utility, and Access to Low-cost (EQUAL) Compute Network as part of the larger AI4D program, with funding from the Government of Canada and FCDO, and additional support from the Gates Foundation, to meet those challenges. Through the AI4D program, the EQUAL Compute Network will support greater access to critical resources such as graphic processing units, data centres and cloud computing for the development of responsible AI. The EQUAL Compute Network will also support research and evidence generation related to sustainable compute infrastructure models and innovations in the Global South.

description.narrative: Accelerating Saving Lives at Birth (SL@B) is an accelerator program that seeks to increase the scale, sustainability, and effectiveness of promising innovations in the Saving Lives at Birth Portfolio - with the overarching goal of improving maternal and newborn health (MNH) outcomes across the globe. Accelerating SL@B innovators strive to first identify and fill gaps left by health systems; working to improve health outcomes that occur before and in the 48 hours after birth, the period when the majority of maternal and newborn deaths occur. The Accelerating SL@B program seeks to help these innovations reach scale through ongoing, individualized coaching and mentoring provided by a team of experts in the innovation and global health spheres. All of the support activities for Accelerating SL@B participants aim to help innovators make progress toward achieving scalability and sustainability. Direct innovator support includes: Coaching from program implementers and other experts in the field of MNH innovation; Tools and resources (i.e. tools that help identify target audience for communication and to develop commercialization plans); In-person events, including one annual workshop and one annual showcase; and Virtual support activities (i.e. webinars and peer community groups).

description.narrative: The purpose of this five-year program is to implement the Congressionally-mandated Child Blindness directive which will expand the availability, accessibility, and quality of eye care services to vulnerable children with limited access to sight-saving services. This purpose will contribute to the overall goal of improving the health and wellbeing of children, especially those in vulnerable populations, increasing economic productivity, and advancing development. Specific goals are: 1) to increase the number of children provided with quality eye care services; and 2) to increase global knowledge of pediatric eye care through innovation and the implementation of best practices. The program will start in late FY18. Project inputs include sub-awards to U.S.-based and non-U.S. based eye care organizations to implement field activities and research; technical assistance to eye care organizations and to other USAID and U.S. Government programs; capacity building and training for small eye care organizations; and technical leadership in the field of global pediatric ophthalmology through research and knowledge sharing efforts. Project outputs include timely issuance of the maximum amount of funds to grants for field activities; strengthened capacity of grantees to meet USAID requirements and performance targets; cross-sectoral linkages and collaborations between USAID and U.S. Government programs where appropriate; expanded innovation in child eye care programming approaches; and integration of evidence-based approaches into large-scale programming and host-country health systems. The Child Blindness Program will promote integration of interventions into existing local health systems and other sector plans and programs (e.g., education) in order to increase long-term sustainability of results and ownership by governments and local actors, and help countries progress on their journey to self-reliance.

title.narrative: Act to End Neglected Tropical Diseases - West

description.narrative: Act to End NTDs | West builds on the successes achieved through previous Agency investments to expand and strengthen national integrated NTD programs to achieve the WHO 2020 NTD goals. This five-year award, managed by FHI360, is intended to support disease-endemic countries to control and/or eliminate NTDs with proven, cost-effective public health interventions to treat and measure treatment impact against seven NTDs: lymphatic filariasis, blinding trachoma, onchocerciasis, schistosomiasis, and three intestinal worms known as soil-transmitted helminths. In addition to continued support toward global disease elimination and control goals, Act to End NTDs | West will focus on helping countries on their journey to self-reliance by supporting them to integrate NTD programs into the broader national health systems and to strengthen technical, operation and financial capacity to operate NTD programs without U.S. foreign assistance funding.

(LAB - Global Development Lab): Reprogrammed funds will meet the Waste Recycling and Toxic Chemicals directive. The will go to an Electronic Waste Recycling program through the Lab's Solar Off Grid Energy (SOGE) team. The program supports project innovation around sustainable battery technology and the recycling infrastructure of the off-grid solar industry. Given the lack of existing company take back programs and e-waste recycling infrastructure across sub-Saharan Africa, this project will focus on the long-term sustainability of solar household system comany product distribution, repair, recycling, and end of life disposal.

title.narrative: Cooperative Development Program (CDP) - Cooperative Resources International

description.narrative: Through the CDP APS mechanism and in support of locally-led development, E3/LS will provide funding to Cooperative Resources International (CRI) to implement cooperative development activities in South Africa and Peru. Specifically, Cooperative Resources International will work with local agricultural cooperatives to improve their management practices, governance and capitalization strategies for increased focus on self-reliance. Additionally, CRI will provide mentoring on farm management for improved agriculture and animal husbandry methods to ensure higher productivity and profitability of local partners. These field-based activities build the capacity of local, democratic institutions and advance the Agency's objectives of local resource mobilization and self-reliance.

Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

title.narrative: S-Higher Education Solution Network (HESN)/ APS - University of Colorado Boulder

description.narrative: (LAB - Global Development Lab): Through the STIP Annual Program Statement (APS), the Lab published an APS aimed at identifying and funding university-based support of cross-cutting development challenges that can be tackled by a "whole of university" approach with our U.S. based and non-U.S. based university partners. Launched in March 2018, the Accelerating Local Potential Addenda to the STIP APS sought to build human and institutional capacity in developing country universities through partnerships with U.S. based universities. After co-creation, four awards were selected that each sought to build capacity and self-reliance by strengthening developing country university institutions. One of the four awards is with the University of Colorado. Globally there is a demand for statisticians and data scientists who can accelerate STIP by collecting, visualizing, and analyzing data and transform the results into data-driven policy recommendations. FY 2018 funding will support the Laboratory for Interdisciplinary Statistical Analysis (LISA) 2020 program to build partnerships between the University of Colorado, Boulder and the University of Ibadan, Nigeria, the University of Calcutta, India, and the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana, in order to create statistical collaboration labs that simultaneously develop statistical and data science capacity and leverage it to solve local development problems.

Through the CDP APS mechanism and in support of locally-led development, E3/LS will provide funding to Global Communities to implement cooperative development activities in Kenya. Specifically, Global Communities will support the adoption and implementation of cooperative law at the county-level, advance research on behavior change and build capacity of local service cooperatives. Additionally, Global Communities will promote inclusion of marginalized communities by focusing on increased access of quality resources tailored with youth and gender considerations. These field-based activities build the capacity of local, democratic institutions and advance the Agency's objectives of local resource mobilization and self-reliance.

title.narrative: Cooperative Development Program (CDP) - Land O'Lakes International Development

description.narrative: Through the CDP APS mechanism and in support of locally-led development, E3/LS will provide funding to Land O'Lakes International to implement cooperative development activities in Rwanda and Malawi. Specifically, Land O'Lakes International will improve cooperative enabling environments through building the capacity of apex associations and advance cooperative business performance of primary and tertiary cooperatives. Additionally, Land O'Lakes will conduct research on locally-led cooperative development and alignment with women and youth engagement. These field-based activities build the capacity of local, democratic institutions and advance the Agency's objectives of local resource mobilization and self-reliance.

Through the CDP APS mechanism and in support of locally-led development, E3/LS will provide funding to HealthPartners to implement cooperative development activities in Uganda. Specifically, HealthPartners will work with new and existing health cooperatives to increase quality healthcare services and insurance to community members. Additionally, HealthPartners will focus on developing skills and creating mentors to promote more female leaders in the health sector. These field-based activities build the capacity of local, democratic institutions and advance the Agency's objectives of local resource mobilization and self-reliance.

Through the CDP APS mechanism and in support of locally-led development, E3/LS will provide funding to Frontier to implement cooperative development activities in Sri Lanka. Specifically, Frontier will work with local spice cooperatives to improve agricultural and processing practices which aim to increase exports and increase smallholder farmer incomes. Additionally, Frontier will promote the inclusion of a marginalized workforce by training youth, women and disabled persons on safe food safety and handling. These field-based activities build the capacity of local, democratic institutions and advance the Agency's objectives of local resource mobilization and self-reliance.

Through the CDP APS mechanism and in support of locally-led development, E3/LS will provide funding to Equal Exchange to implement cooperative development activities in Mexico, Peru, Guatemala and Paraguay. Specifically, Equal Exchange will work with local agricultural cooperatives to improve their quality, productivity, and processing of cacao and coffee to ensure increased exports and higher prices for commodities back to smallholder farmers. Additionally, Equal Exchange will work to increase member equity in each agricultural cooperative to ensure long-term sustainability. These field-based activities build the capacity of local, democratic institutions and advance the Agency's objectives of local resource mobilization and self-reliance.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Innovation Lab for Fish

description.narrative: Purpose: To conduct research on fish to contribute to the needs of small scale fish producers and processors, and stakeholders along fish value chain. The FTFIL for Fish will conduct research along the aquaculture value chain using a country-led process to define the program's research priorities. The project draws on the expertise of US universities and developing country research institutions to address the GFSS goal of reducing global hunger, malnutrition, and poverty. Activities: Research across the biophysical and social sciences on fish with a global program scope. The research project will focus on research activities and results; increase collaboration between the Management Entity, Asia, Africa and Central America partners; explore collaboration opportunities with other Innovation Labs as well as private industry partnerships in the area of fish meal replacement in fish feed, fish genetic improvement, nutrition, food safety, income generation, gender and youth.

This activity facilitates the engagement of highly skilled volunteers in advancing development by building the capacity of government and/or community authorities to manage areas designated for biodiversity conservation, as well as advising institutions involved in developing conservation policies, enforcing conservation laws, or promoting transparency and accountability of conservation actions. The volunteer conservation experts assess needs, recommend solutions, and conduct analyses or peer-to-peer training to improve practices and capacity of natural resource management agencies. Using skilled volunteers to build conservation capacity is a Congressional interest. This flexible, cost effective assistance complements mission programs in Thailand, Peru, Colombia and Kenya, and supports Embassy interest in Mongolia.

title.narrative: Act to End Neglected Tropical Diseases - East

description.narrative: Act to End NTDs | East builds on the successes achieved through previous Agency investments to expand and strengthen national integrated NTD programs to achieve the WHO 2020 NTD goals. This five-year award, managed by RTI International, is intended to support disease-endemic countries to control and/or eliminate NTDs with proven, cost-effective public health interventions to treat and measure treatment impact against seven NTDs: lymphatic filariasis, blinding trachoma, onchocerciasis, schistosomiasis, and three intestinal worms known as soil-transmitted helminths. In addition to continued support toward global disease elimination and control goals, Act to End NTDs | East will focus on helping countries on their journey to self-reliance by supporting them to integrate NTD programs into the broader national health systems and to strengthen technical, operation and financial capacity to operate NTD programs without U.S. foreign assistance funding. This centrally managed agreement will support Bangladesh, DRC, Ethiopia, Haiti, Indonesia, Laos, Mozambique, Nepal, Nigeria, Philippines, Tanzania, Uganda, and Vietnam.

Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Nutrition in Complex Environments (ONCE; Prime: Tufts)

description.narrative: Purpose: BFS, along with the Bureau for Global Health and the Office of Food For Peace co-designed an Agency-wide, applied research activity to support innovations in the prevention and treatment of nutrition vulnerabilities in complex environments. The activity is in support of the Agency's Multi-Sectoral Nutrition Strategy and contributes to the Agency's objectives under Ending Preventable Child and Maternal Deaths (EPCMD), and the Global Food Security Strategy (GFSS). The activity is part of the partnership USAID announced at the 2017 Global Nutrition Summit and builds on the Agency's strong history of investments in effective and scalable interventions that prevent and treat undernutrition. It will contribute to USAID's understanding of how to address poor nutrition in complex environments to strengthen resilience in areas of recurrent crises. Activities: Research will take place in the Karamoja region of Uganda, where chronic and acute malnutrition and food security remain a substantial challenge. ONCE will assess, monitor and evaluate an innovative multi-sectoral approach designed to reduce drivers of child malnutrition. Specifically, the activity will conduct formative research, program intervention and process monitoring; an impact evaluation; and a sustainability assessment. This research is innovative as it focuses on identifying implementation best practices to improve global understanding of how to implement high-quality, effective, sustainable, multi-sectoral programming in complex environments. A research uptake strategy will be employed to link research and learning to policy and practice.This activity is led by Tufts University, who is well-situated to achieve the activity goals, as Tufts has principal investigators with unique expertise in nutrition in complex environments as well as extensive experience in managing successful research partnerships. Tufts has a Uganda office and four active studies in the country.

description.narrative: Purpose: The Bureau for Food Security along with the Bureau for Global Health and the Office of Food For Peace co-designed an Agency-wide, applied research activity to support innovations in the prevention and treatment of nutrition vulnerabilities in complex environments. The activity is in support of the Agency's Multi-Sectoral Nutrition Strategy and contributes to the Agency's objectives under Ending Preventable Child and Maternal Deaths (EPCMD), and the Global Food Security Strategy (GFSS). The activity is part of the partnership USAID announced at the 2017 Global Nutrition Summit and builds on the Agency's strong history of investments in effective and scalable interventions that prevent and treat undernutrition. It will contribute to USAID's understanding of how to address poor nutrition in complex environments to strengthen resilience in areas of recurrent crises. Activities: This activity employs development research in regions of Ethiopia where chronic and acute malnutrition and food security remain a substantial challenge. Formative research will be conducted to inform a package of supply and demand side behavior change interventions to improve consumption of animal-source foods (ASFs). This package will be tested via a cluster-randomized control trial (cRCT); impact will be measured through key purchase, consumption, and behavior-related indicators. The results from the applied research will provide important insights into the most effective mix of incentives to support year-round access to affordable, nutritious diets in complex environments where local markets are not well-developed. This activity is led by John Snow, Inc. (JSI) with the International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) as a principal partner. JSI and IFPRI both have extensive experience in Ethiopia and provide a unique mix of local and global technical expertise in the technical topic and the research methodologies.

(Ghana): The Quality Services for Health activity will provide technical assistance to the Ministry of Health and its agencies to plan and implement health system strengthening activities to build self-sustaining local systems. Using FY 2021 funds, this activity will support sustainable, quality, patient-centered services through an integrated, cross cutting approach and will particularly target maternal and child health, family planning and reproductive health, nutrition and infection prevention and control with WASH Quality Improvement (QI) to improve critical health outcomes. It will support the adoption of behaviors at the policy, management, and service provider levels to ensure quality health services. The activity will support relevant coordination mechanisms across Ministry of Health agencies to implement quality improvement initiatives and create strong linkages with regulatory bodies to enhance the regulatory environment within the national quality improvement framework. Further, the activity will support the Government of Ghana to strengthen leadership and governance of quality management structures and processes; improve institutional effectiveness of regulatory agencies to ensure quality service delivery; and improve monitoring, evaluation, and learning for continuous health system strengthening. The activity will utilize capacity building; institutional strengthening, process establishment and improvement; and enabling environment approaches to ensure country ownership and sustainability.

title.narrative: Integrated Health Systems - Health Workforce Management

description.narrative: (Nigeria): USAID/Nigeria's buy-in to USAID's Integrated Health Systems (IHS) mechanism supports the establishment of a cost-effective, well-trained and motivated health workforce that will contribute to improved management of reproductive health, family planning, maternal, child and newborn health conditions and increased responsiveness to community health needs. .The activity offers a state-of-the-art approach for advancing Nigeria's health workforce agenda through tailored, state-level technical assistance. Interventions will target the focus states of Bauchi, Sokoto, Kebbi, Ebonyi, and the Federal Capital Territory ensuring that technical assistance meets context-specific priorities for local human resources and health systems. Interventions will focus on support to state governments to improve the quality of training for the health workforce, strengthen the health workforce information system, improve health workforce governance and management, and strengthen local capacity for learning, documentation, and research. With FY 2021 funds, the activity will support the establishment and strengthening of key human resources for health governance platforms,, strengthen continuing education systems and human resource information systems, provide technical assistance to develop and implement action plans, policies, and strategic plans to improve these training institutions and system platforms, and support initiatives to improve the availability of health workforce for primary health care service delivery. ...

This is a new purchase order under the Climate BPA to produce Greenhouse Gas Factsheets. The country and regional factsheets summarize existing information on greenhouse gas emissions and country priorities as they relate to various development sectors. USAID staff use these factsheets to inform programming, particularly the development of Country and Regional Development Cooperation Strategies. Countries and other partners also use these factsheets to inform their own development plans and actions. As of July 2017, these factsheets have been downloaded 6,500 times. The factsheets help missions and others consider opportunities to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, which can be achieved with technologies developed and/or manufactured by U.S. businesses, e.g., clean energy technologies.

title.narrative: AWE Call Orders and Knowledge Management

description.narrative: Primary responsibilities for overall management include overall quality assurance for services and deliverables for AWE Call Orders and knowledge management; identification, contracting and supervision of consultants and/or personnel engaged in the AWE; communication with the COR, missions, partners, and relevant stakeholders to ensure responsive, timely, and high-quality services; monitoring and evaluation; reporting; and general administration. It is anticipated that AWE management, the COR, and the requesting entity for specific Call Orders in AWE Components 1-3 will coordinate to ensure technical quality, client satisfaction, feasibility, and contribution to AWE objectives and learning. Knowledge-management will emphasize internal knowledge management of continually capturing and applying learning throughout AWE Call Orders across all three Components of the AWE. Technical approaches to knowledge management should align with USAID practices of collaboration, learning, and adaption to capture, organize, and apply lessons learned during AWE implementation to other AWE Call Orders, within and across AWE Components. Externally-facing knowledge management will leverage existing Feed the Future, USAID, and food security sector platforms.

description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): EngageHCD is a contracting vehicle available to USAID's Bureau for Global Health and Missions to procure technical assistance on state-of-the-art human-centered design (HCD) services and explore how to scale up activities to encourage uptake and adherence to care seeking behavior. HCD is a discipline that applies a specific mindset and skill set for creative problem solving by placing the values, needs, and behavior of people at the center of our work. HCD approaches leverages design thinking expertise to generate insights, co-create prototypes, test options, and iterate solutions hand-in-hand with the target end-users. There are a range of specializations within design, such as experience design, service delivery design, communication design, and product design. HCD is used to develop informed, inclusive, purposeful, compelling, and innovative solutions that better fit into people's lives as well as into the broader systems that they live in. Examples of this work include driving demand for the use of chlorhexidine to increase newborn health and increasing the uptake of the dapivirine ring (DPV ring) for HIV prevention. HCD expertise is used to support the development and adaptation of tools to encourage uptake and correct use of the DPV ring-and other rings in the pipeline-among young women by situating its use within their daily values, needs, and lives. HCD is also being used to adapt and pilot an oral PrEP campaign that reframes oral PrEP from a medical product to a fashion or beauty product that can easily fit into a young woman's daily ritual. In another effort, HCD is being used to explore the potential of alternative private sector channels for PrEP, driven by the needs of the end users and pain points they experience with current offerings.

title.narrative: Kuboresha Afya Mitaani: Urban MNCH Project

description.narrative: Kuboresha Afya Mitaani project (KAM), also known as the Urban MNCH Project, is using implementation research to better understand and improve maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) outcomes for women and children living in the informal settlements of Kawangware and Mathare North in Nairobi, Kenya. In addition to strengthening approaches that will increase demand generation and delivery of quality MNCH services, KAM will also explore ways to improve the linkages between facilities and the city's regulatory system to improve high-quality, live-saving services in both public and private health facilities. The project will explore a 'quality ecosystem' model to improve health in the informal settlements by integrating typically siloed actors in the quality of care space in Nairobi, including women and families, communities, facilities, health providers, health regulators and actors in WASH and air pollution. This work is not only intended to improve outcomes for almost 60,000 of Nairobi s most vulnerable women and children, but it will also use real-time learning to plan and catalyze a sustainable approach across Kenya s largest city, working in partnership with key public and private sector stakeholders that can inform efforts in other African urban contexts. It will provide a template for African cities to understand how to build successful programs to address the unique challenges of MNCH in informal settlements.

Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Innovation Lab for Crop Improvement

description.narrative: The Feed the Future Innovation Lab for Crop Improvement (ILCI) will be an integrated research and delivery program with multidisciplinary expertise at the cutting edge of agricultural development, from plant breeding and machine learning to quantitative genetics and gender inclusion. The USAID MVDP has been successful in building strategic partnerships with some of the most capable malaria vaccine groups in the world. title.narrative: CA: Virus Resistant Cassava for Africa (VIRCA) Plus

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Resilience and Food Security (RFS)): .Purpose: To implement the Science, Technology and Innovation elements of the Global Food Security Act, a portfolio of research programs across the biophysical and social sciences has been developed that is central to advancing novel solutions that support global efforts to reduce hunger, poverty, and malnutrition. As part of the Feed the Future Agricultural Biotechnology for Food Security Program, this award contributes to these goals by developing and taking to scale agricultural biotechnology products that advance food security objectives...Activities: This activity advances the development, regulatory approval, and commercialization of Genetically Engineered (GE) cassava varieties that are virus-resistant and nutritionally biofortified with enhanced levels of iron and zinc. Under this latest phase of the activity, the Danforth Center is working in partnership with researchers in African partner countries to complete the biosafety regulatory application and release process for locally adapted GE cassava varieties (developed and tested under prior phases of the project), as well as to initiate pilot-scale commercialization of GE cassava products in Kenya in partnership with local seed entrepreneurs. The project also includes accompanying capacity-development support to enable partner-country innovation and market systems to develop and disseminate biotechnology products that address food security challenges-ultimately enhancing the productivity, resilience, and nutrition of smallholders..Benefiting Countries: Kenya, Rwanda, Nigeria, Uganda, with potential expansion to Malawi and Mozambique..
Support higher education institutions in helping solve complex development problems through use of research, innovation, and training.

title.narrative: ID: Indigenous Peoples Alliance for Rights and Development (IPARD)

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Inclusive Growth, Partnerships, and Innovation (IPI)): The Indigenous Peoples' Alliance for Rights and Development is a public-private partnership to secure rights, enhance capabilities, and create self-determined economic opportunities for Indigenous Peoples worldwide. This partnership harnesses the strengths and experiences of a collective, multi-sector network to empower Indigenous Peoples' organizations and catalyze an enabling environment where Indigenous Peoples can manage, develop, and govern their own territories based on the principles of self-determined development, traditional practices, natural resource management, and respect for their customary rights. This program contributes to the National Security Strategy and the Joint Strategic Plan by helping to create a prosperous world through supporting inclusive economic growth, supporting the dignity of individuals, empowering local actors to seek enduring solutions to their development challenges, and improving and adapting policy and foreign assistance to advance the inclusion of Indigenous peoples. This IM implements the Indigenous People directive/earmark.

title.narrative: Achieve Onchocerciasis Elimination in the Americas (Achieve OEA)

description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): Funds will support the complete elimination of onchocerciasis (River Blindness) in the Americas. Onchocerciasis only remains in one area of the Americas, signifying a 95% reduction of disease. With 5% burden remaining, Achieve OEA provides technical and programmatic assistance to implement mass treatment campaigns with the goal of interrupting onchocerciasis transmission and achieving full elimination of this disease in the Americas. USAID has supported the control and elimination of the most common neglected tropical diseases since 2006. $742,582 of FY24 funds will be attriubed to Achieve OEA activities in Central America, Guatemala. ..USAID support through Achieve OEA helps to provide training to indigenous health agents (IHAs), as well as increase their numbers and gender balance. IHAs play a critical role in the program by providing directly, or helping health teams to provide, ivermectin treatments to prevent onchocerciasis. They offer cultural knowledge, translation skills, and serve as guides in the Amazon Rain Forest. Support will also fund an anthropologist to help determine culturally appropriate ways to increase IHA participation, particularly female IHAs who currently make up about 5% of all IHAs. .

title.narrative: Innovate FP: Expanding Options, Enhancing Choice

description.narrative: The goal of Innovate FP is to expand desirable, affordable, quality contraceptive options to enable women to better meet their changing needs and desires throughout their reproductive lives. Despite recent progress, more than 214 million women of reproductive age, who would like to delay, space, or limit their next pregnancy, do not use modern contraceptives, and many do not use methods for product-related reasons. Innovative solutions are essential to address product gaps. Activities under Innovate FP will build on the current USAID-funded Envision FP project and FHI 360 s broader contraceptive technology work. Through Innovate FP, FHI 360 will seek to strengthen and build partnerships to improve contraceptive options; advance novel approaches with potential for fewer side effects; respond to product-related issues; and address existing gaps in knowledge and practice.

sector.narrative: Basic life skills for youth and adults

description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): The goal of Project UChoose is to advance the research, development, and understanding of safe, effective, and affordable contraceptive methods which will better enable women to make decisions around their family planning needs. Project activities include developing a versatile, long-acting, biodegradable pellet system and inserter that would better meet user needs and preferences, while minimizing the need for removal procedures which can place a burden on clients and health systems. Activities also include completion and data analysis for a clinical trial evaluating the mucosal impact of contraceptive use and developing clinical and laboratory methods to evaluate novel contraceptive safety endpoints. Project UChoose also includes a technology incubator aimed at generating proof-of-concept data for promising new contraceptive technologies. Activities in the incubator include development of a 3D-printed intrauterine device and pre-clinical effectiveness studies of novel non-hormonal compounds. The project focuses on collecting new data on the impact of highly effective contraceptives on women's health and strengthening research capacity in Africa.

title.narrative: Accelerate Womens Entrepreneurship for Peace and Prosperity in Mindanao (Accelerate) Project

description.narrative: The Accelerate project will work to support all three pillars of the W-GDP. Pillar 1: Women Prospering in the Workforce: by increasing womens labor force participation in Mindanao, and advancement in the workplace by providing women with quality training and support, so they can create businesses and create well-paying jobs in their local economies. Pillar 2: Women Succeeding as Entrepreneurs is the main thrust of Accelerate, by increasing women entrepreneurs access to financing, market opportunities, and training to establish and grow their businesses. The project will also support Pillar 3: Women Enabled in the Economy: by working towards an enabling environment for womens economic empowerment and economic participation, by reducing barriers and enhancing protections in policies, regulations and practices.

description.narrative: The goal of the Greater Internet Freedom (GIF) program is to advance Internet Freedom in the countries in which it works by ensuring that digital security capacities, data awareness, and activism on behalf of an open, interoperable, reliable, and secure Internet are available, adaptive and integrated into the operation of independent media and civil society. To achieve this goal, GIF has two objectives - to enhance digital security for civil society and media and to increase citizen engagement in internet governance.

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Resilience and Food Security (RFS)): Purpose: To implement the Science, Technology and Innovation elements of the Global Food Security Act, a portfolio of research programs across the biophysical and social sciences have been developed and are central to advancing novel solutions that support global efforts to reduce hunger, poverty, and malnutrition. This five-year program seeks to support research for technology development and testing of new, improved animal health interventions such as vaccines and diagnostic tests to improve the control of East Coast fever (ECF), a devastating disease of cattle. The program will also build the capacity of a local university to conduct laboratory-based animal health research and train a new generation of animal health scientists. The activity draws on the expertise of US universities and developing country research institutions to address the GFSS goal of reducing global hunger, malnutrition, and poverty. $1 million of funding within this IM contributes to meeting the required "Research and Development" directive of $148.8 million and the required "Feed the Future Innovation Labs" sub-directive of $58 million...Activities: The program will complete the equipping of the newly refurbished laboratory at the University of Nairobi in Kenya, engage in field-based and laboratory research to develop and innovate East Coast Fever diagnostic tools and vaccines for future scaling..Benefitting Countries: Kenya..
The activity seeks to develop an insect-resistant, bioengineered cowpea to improve nutrition and food security in Africa.

title.narrative: CR: FTF Building a Resilient Future

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Resilience and Food Security (RFS)): Purpose: The purpose of the FTF Building a Resilient Future Project (also referred to as the Global Resilience Partnership (GRP)) is to advance the adoption and implementation of USAID resilience key principles and realize the Agency's desired results through more effective resilience programming. ..Activities: GRP is guided by the USAID Resilience Policy with a focus on three areas: (1) Building a more robust and globally recognized resilience community of practice; (2) Policy convening and influence to advance USAID resilience objectives; and (3) Increasing access to and application of resilience-oriented knowledge, solutions, expertise, and best practices through an online platform..Benefitting Countries: The Resilience Focus Countries as well as other Countries with USAID Missions integrating resilience approaches to their development and humanitarian portfolio
Reduce the transmission and impact of HIV/AIDS through support for prevention, care and treatment programs.

title.narrative: ID: Learning, Acting and Building for Rehabilitation in Health Systems (ReLAB-HS)

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Inclusive Growth, Partnerships, and Innovation (IPI)): This activity's overall goal is to support the development of health systems that are responsive to growing needs for rehabilitation across the lifespan. The activity will focus on service delivery and workforce strengthening, policy and prioritization, drivers to integrate rehabilitation in health systems, building an understanding on rehabilitation, and conducting and sharing research, evaluations, and learning.. In addition, the activity will continue to fund and provide technical assistance to accelerator grants to support sustainability of efforts. In line with the National Security Strategy and the Joint Strategic Plan, the activity helps to ensure accountability to U.S. taxpayers by strengthening local systems to support the sustainability of development investments and address barriers to equal access and opportunity. This IM implements the Leahy War Victim Fund directive/earmark.

title.narrative: Collective Action to Reduce Gender-Based Violence (CARE-GBV)

description.narrative: CARE-GBV is centered on strengthening USAIDs collective prevention and response, or collective action in GBV development programming across USAID. The activity will achieve this strengthening by supporting USAIDs Gender Equality and Womens Empowerment (GenDev) hub in the development of guidelines, strategic plans, training, and professional networking support. To that end, CARE-GBV is working to accomplish five key objectives: (1) Develop and disseminate foundational elements for integrated and standalone GBV programming in development contexts (2) Strengthen prevention and response programming on harmful GBV practices, including female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C) and child, early, and forced marriage (CEFM), across different sectors through convening workshops, implementation plans, and learning agenda development (3) Create knowledge products to strengthen GBV programming (4) Strengthen the USAID GBV community of practice and donor coordination in GBV programming (5) Award small grants to new, local, and under-utilized partners to promote capacity building and learning focused on GBV staff and organizational wellness and resiliency.

title.narrative: Analytic Task on Authoritarian Resurgence & Influence (ATARI)

description.narrative: The Analytic Task on Authoritarian Resurgence and Influence (ATARI) will develop and pilot a new diagnostic tool for assessing Resurgent Authoritarianism and Influence in USAID partner countries and will work collaboratively with target USAID Missions and stakeholders to formulate effective programmatic responses. As an interrelated component, ATARI will also synthesize the growing body of research and evidence on Chinese, Russian and other authoritarian influence operations, identify knowledge and data gaps, and facilitate networking and information exchange among members of a growing community of RAI researchers and practitioners.

title.narrative: Jobs to End Poverty: Evidence from Bangladesh

description.narrative: With an Evidence Generation grant from USAID's Development Innovation Ventures, the London School of Economics (LSE) is running a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of PROSPER, a skill development program operated by the NGO BRAC. PROSPER participants receive classroom as well as hands-on training where they are matched to an employer in a high-demand trade. During the trial, BRAC is offering PROSPER at different price points, including a deferred payment option in some cases, to young workers across 30 locations.

Climate change-induced environmental stressesincluding drought, extreme temperatures, and soil salinizationthreaten food security all over the world, with developing countries expected to be the most significantly impacted. Smallholder farmers are particularly vulnerable, including nearly 120 million subsistence farmers in India who live on less than $2 per day. To improve crop resilience and yields under these stressful conditions, Washington state-based biotech company Adaptive Symbiotic Technologies (AST) developed BioEnsure, a low-cost fungus-based seed treatment that increases the ability of plants to access water and nutrients in the soil. Unlike many products meant to improve agricultural productivity, BioEnsure requires almost no behavior change by farmers, making it an easily adoptable solution that can be applied to both new seeds and seeds from previously harvested plants. In a USAID-supported pilot program, smallholder farmers in India increased their yields by over 50 percent on average. With support from Development Innovation Ventures (DIV), AST is conducting peer reviewed trials and exploring new sales and distribution strategies, business models, and pricing structures to demonstrate a commercial pathway to scale that expects to reach over 100,000 smallholder farmers in India over three years. DIV support aims to de-risk future investment in AST's Indian operations and attract private capital, while helping smallholder farmers in Rajasthan access this innovative technology.

title.narrative: DRG: PIDR Global Labor Program - Platform for Organizing by Workers for Empowerment and Recognition (GLP-POWER)

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Development, Democracy, and Innovation (D): The Global Labor Program - Platform for Organizing by Workers for Empowerment and Recognition (GLP-POWER) is implemented by a coalition of global, regional, and local organizations led by Solidar Suisse. GLP-POWER tests innovative means of organizing migrant and informal workers, who are particularly vulnerable to labor rights abuses and difficult to reach. These innovations include the use of technology (alongside in-person methods) to connect workers to each other, and to provide resources to assist them in protecting their rights. The project also conducts research in partnership with workers to put them in the lead in developing solutions to the challenges they face..With FY 2022 funds for Year-2 of the activity, GLP-POWER will build on the successful initial stages of development of the technology platform from Year-1, by adding additional modules, resources, and other types of content, and by socializing the platform among end-users while capturing feedback for continuous improvement. By doing so, vulnerable workers, and the organizations that represent and/or serve them, will be better able to access legal aid, migrants support, women's groups, and psychosocial services..GLP-POWER directly contributes to the Multilateral Partnership for Organizing, Worker Empowerment, and Rights (M-POWER) initiative, which is a key deliverable of the Presidential Initiative for Democratic Renewal (PIDR) that USAID collaborates on with the Department of Labor and U.S. Department of State's Bureau for Democracy, Rights, and Labor (DRL)..

title.narrative: ID: Center for Victims of Torture- Helping Survivors Heal

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Inclusive Growth, Partnerships, and Innovation (IPI)): The Helping Suvivors Heal activity enhances the effectiveness of local service providers for survivors of torture and build mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) workforce capacity to expand access to quality, evidence-based services adapted to local contexts, with explicit attention to gender and social inclusion. The activity is a collaborative partnerships between the Center for Victims of Torture and 12 local providers of MHPSS services to survivors of torture in the Global South. In FY 2024,a particular focus will be on the 12 partners to provide organizational diversity (e.g., size, client population, geography) and enrich cross partner learning and project impact, but allow for deep and holistic capacity support. The program contributes to the Agency's development and foreign policy objectives by - among other things - improving well-being and resilience, and promoting peace and stability. This IM implements the Victims of Torture directive/earmark.

(USAID Bureau for Inclusive Growth, Partnerships, and Innovation (IPI)): The purpose of this activity is to build the capacity of locally owned and democratically run businesses through the provision of specialized technical assistance and legal and regulatory reform. The design of this activity was informed by prior program evaluations, sectoral analyses and a co-creation process informed by Mission-based technical specialists, local cooperatives and credit unions, and implementing partners. Funding provided to this IM contributes to delivering on the overall objectives of the global Cooperative Development Program earmark, valued at $18.5 million.

title.narrative: A Media Experiment to Reduce Intimate Partner Violence in Bangladesh

description.narrative: Although intimate partner violence (IPV) is a pervasive problem affecting one in three women worldwide, its drivers are complex and not well understood. Bangladesh has one of the highest rates of IPV in the world. Exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, IPV has increased in frequency and prevalence. However, few interventions have been shown to meaningfully improve the social norms or behaviors of male abusers. To reduce abusive behavior perpetrated by men, the implementing partner will design a six-episode edutainment drama series focused on resilience based on cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to improve anger management and nonviolent coping skills. The implementing partner will refine the content, work with a production company to produce the series, and conduct a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to test the effectiveness of each set of episodes in public and private settings. The trial will measure the impact of the interventions on beliefs about IPV, nonviolent coping skills, rates of victimization, and the cost-effectiveness of this low-cost edutainment approach compared to in-person group therapy. This studypossibly the first study of a CBT-based edutainment interventionis expected to reveal key drivers of IPV, identify potential solutions that are relatively inexpensive to scale, and to inform future development programs and policies globally.
This partnership was launched under USAIDs Digital Invest program to support the sustainable growth and expansion of competitive internet service providers (ISPs) in emerging markets.

Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

This partnership was launched under USAIDs Digital Invest program, a partnership initiative between USAIDs Innovation, Technology, and Research Hub, the Gender Equality & Women's Empowerment Hub (GenDev), and the State Department, under the U.S. Digital Connectivity and Cybersecurity Partnership (DCCP). The Digital Invest program has two objectives: 1) Support the sustainable growth and expansion of competitive internet service providers (ISPs) in emerging markets, and 2) Support the sustainable growth and expansion of competitive financial technology companies in emerging markets. Integra Partners is an impact focused venture capital fund manager that makes investments in early-stage technology companies across Southeast Asia, with a secondary focus on South Asia. Integras mission is to drive impact and inclusion in Southeast Asia across financial services, insurance, and digital health with an aim to give every person and business in the region the ability to manage and improve their financial and physical health digitally and at a reasonable cost.

title.narrative: DRG: Civil Society and Media Strengthening - Stronger Together and Advancing in New Directions (CSM-STAND) / Africa and the Middle East

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Development, Democracy, and Innovation (D): The purpose of CSM-STAND is to identify and foster effective approaches to strengthen civic engagement and independent media and increase the use of these approaches by USAID Missions, civil society, and independent media in support of DRG and other development results. CSM-STAND strengthens civil society and media capacities to represent citizen interests; defend institutions of democracy; hold governments and private sector actors accountable through advocacy, oversight, and outreach; prevent conflict; and promote resilience. FY2022 funds will build on past efforts to generate learning materials and practical tools to improve Missions civil society, media, labor, and youth related activity design and management. CSM-STAND activities will produce technical materials and facilitate engagement of relevant thinkers and practitioners as a means to share information and promote regional and cross-Mission learning. CSM-STAND will support technical resources that advance the integration of pluralist approaches into the design and implementation of programming, the development of an online learning platform, and implementation of a global learning agenda that will promote the accumulation of evidence, peer learning, and trans-regional collaboration across the civil society and media sector. The learning agenda will focus on improving interventions that advance the safety and wellbeing of journalists, activists and organizations; strengthen networks, collaboration and collective action across borders; and increase integrity of information and trustworthiness of media and civic institutions. title.narrative: DRG: Democratic Elections and Political Processes (DEPP) Leader with Associate (LWA)

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Development, Democracy, and Innovation (D): With FY 2022 funds, the Democratic Elections and Political Processes (DEPP) Leader with Associate (LWA) Awards will support three priority areas of programming under the Leader award: (a) rapid and flexible response (RFR) activities address unanticipated needs, emerging opportunities and critical gaps in programming. Rapid response activities can enable a quick start up of activities in a time sensitive and rapidly evolving situation, (b) targeted interventions or pilot programs to encourage innovations, creative solutions and/or target distinct issues or solve particular problems including in countries not undergoing transitions, (c) technical leadership activities to conduct innovative research resulting in the development of widely disseminated practical user-friendly guides, tools, and training publications in the field of elections and political transitions. This may include applied research, knowledge management activities, and evaluation of programs and experiences across regions to identify best practices and lessons learned. Technical leadership may also include convening events to share and disseminate lessons learned throughout the development community and among relevant stakeholders. The LWAs field-oriented approach aligns with the Development, Democracy, and Innovation Bureau's focus on serving Missions.

title.narrative: Interactive Mobile Support for Frontline Workers Promoting Breastfeeding

description.narrative: More than four million frontline workers (FLWs) serve over one billion of the world's poorest. FLW programs reach broadly over remote and underserved regions, and ensuring that workers have sufficient and consistent knowledge, skills, and support is challenging. Digital innovations that enhance and complement FLWs knowledge have the potential to be highly cost-effective, scalable ways to improve infant and child wellbeing, especially when compared with traditional multi-day in-person training programs. To support FLWs to provide the most important information to new mothers during home visits, the implementing partner is designing an app that uses behavior change techniques to prepare FLWs to talk about breastfeeding with their clients in a culturally sensitive way. Drawing from behavioral science, the app uses automatic notifications, simple clinical algorithms, and demonstration videos to help FLWs identify and address breastfeeding challenges. User testing includes one-on-one and small group testing with FLWs and community members in Phase 1, and complete training and app testing with a larger number of randomly selected FLWs in Phase 2. Although the app is designed to be used by FLWs, the overall approach can be translated to other sectors, particularly where an intermediary aims to facilitate behavior change. If the app is shown to be effective, it could be scaled up to reach the 100,000 FLWs across Pakistan.

It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. title.narrative: Motomeds: Providing Essential Nighttime Healthcare to Children

description.narrative: Diarrhea, acute respiratory infection, and malaria are the leading causes of mortality for children under five, even though inexpensive treatments may be available. Poor communities struggle to access treatment for childrenespecially at night when treatment options are scarce. Rapid treatment can prevent the need for increased interventions such as emergency care that may be limited, expensive, and risky. The University of Floridas MotoMeds program is a pediatric nighttime telemedicine and medication delivery service that provides effective, low-cost treatments to young children in need of after-hours healthcare. MotoMeds offers free access to a nighttime telephone medical line to triage cases, recommend treatment, and when necessary, order medicine and a household assessment delivered quickly by motorcycles. Since 2019, Motomeds has been serving a population of nearly 18,000 children in 50 rural neighborhoods in Haiti. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, the University of Florida will expand MotoMeds with a pilot project in Accra, Ghana in partnership with the Ghanaian National Ambulance Service. This pilot aims to reduce mortality among children under five, and to inform future replications of MotoMeds in Ghana and other countries.

description.narrative: The purpose of Donors and Locally Led Development: Transforming relationships for strong and resilient communities program is to understand : (1) how a donors role, expectations and conditionalities impact locally led development and (2) how this understanding can be deployed towards developing effective and impactful development projects.

title.narrative: Addressing Vaccine Misinformation with an Inoculation Chatbot

description.narrative: To protect populations against viral misinformation, the implementing partner used behavioral science to design an inoculation chatbot, through which interactive software guides users through narrative, games, and experiential learning that pre-bunks misinformation, equipping users with the skills required to be less susceptible to misinformation. Misinformation about the SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) pandemicranging from rumors about false cures to harmful conspiracieshas spread rapidly through populations via social media and other channels. This spread poses a serious challenge for public health officials working to protect their populations with effective, safe vaccines. Vaccine hesitancy remains strong in Uzbekistan, with only 47.9 percent of its 34 million residents vaccinated against COVID-19. The inoculation chatbot will be a free service and cost less to run than traditional media and short message services. The implementing partner is partnering with the Government of Uzbekistan to pilot the chatbot, and will conduct a randomized controlled trial to identify whether the chatbot helps users better spot manipulation techniques, reduces willingness to share manipulation techniques, and improves willingness to be vaccinated. Through the power of behavioral science, the inoculation chatbot has the potential to protect millions of people against a broad range of misinformation.

description.narrative: Ensuring the viability of public interest media is central to the aim of USAID's democracy, human rights, and governance strategy to support the consolidation of inclusive and accountable democracies to advance freedom, dignity, and development. At the December 2021 summit for democracy, the U.S. government will announce several marquee deliverables to support democracy worldwide, including a deliverable to support independent media and the free flow of information. to that end, the usg will be making a substantial investment, via a grant assistance award, to a new international fund for public interest media, a sponsored project of rockefeller philanthropy advisors. The three main aims of the international fund for public interest media are to: increase the resources available to support independent public interest media in low and middle income countries deploy those resources effectively to both sustain public interest journalism institutions whilst ensuring maximum other revenue is generated and the markets are not distorted develop or contribute to the development of systemic solutions to the current business model challenge by deploying financial, political and knowledge capital.

title.narrative: Feed the FutureInnovation LabforSoybean Value Chain Research

description.narrative: the purpose of the new soybean value chain research (svcr) innovation lab (il) is to facilitate the development and dissemination of evidence-based technologies and practices for widespread adoption and build the capacity of public-private partners across soy market systems in sub-saharan africa (ssa). soybean produced by african countries is 1% of the total world production and the domestic need for food and feed is met by importing over four million metric tons (mt) of soybean grain and its products. soybean grain yield (around 1 mt/ha) is 39% lower than world average and 68% lower than that of the usa. constraints that contribute to such low yields are a) biotic and abiotic stresses, b) narrow germplasm adapted to tropical environments, c) limited access to quality seeds for farmers including financing, d) inadequate agronomic practices, e) absence of small-scale farm mechanization, and f) inadequate market linkages. key results or outcomes expected are: a) soy breeding programs of national agriculture research systems (nars) and cgiar in ssa modernized and use new tools and methods to resolve biotic and abiotic stresses, b) improved soybean varieties with enhanced grain yield (genetic gain) developed and deployed, c) improved soy management practices developed and input bundling for different production systems generated, d) affordable small-scale farm mechanization, e) enhanced soy utilization for food and feed, f) economic impact of soybean known for selected ftf countries, and g) soy public-private research for development (r4d) networks strengthened. this program is designed to identify and launch a new feed the future innovation lab focused on soybean value chain research and capacity development at the smallholder and food-feed systems levels. title.narrative: GenDev - buy-in ITR - Women in the Digital Economy Fund (WiDEF) (GSMA)

description.narrative: (USAID Bureau for Inclusive Growth, Partnerships, and Innovation (IPI)): The Women in the Digital Economy Fund (WiDEF) is a joint effort between USAID and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation to accelerate progress on closing the gender digital divide. As part of the $50 million 3-year commitment of Gender Equity and Equality Action (GEEA) fund resources, GenDev's FY24 funds will be used to accelerate progress to close the gender digital divide by scaling evidence-based, proven solutions, including women-led solutions that improve women's livelihoods, economic security, and resilience. USAID funding will support programs that strengthen digital access and affordability; increase the design and development, especially women-led development, of relevant products and tools; increase digital literacy and skills training; address online safety and security; and increase sex-disaggregated data and research. This approach has been determined to best achieve the activity's theory of change, which is for WiDEF to: 1) help public, private sector, and civil society stakeholders to become better aware of the complex set of root causes of gender-digital inequities; 2) USAID, in collaboration with its partners, learn about the evidence-based solutions to address these inequalities; 3) for USAID and its partners to provide direct and aligned funding to to local entities to enable them to scale up these proven solutions; and 4) for the cohesive longer term impact of USAID's and its direct and aligned partners' activities to accelerate progress to close the gender digital divide, thereby improving women's livelihoods, economic security, and resilience.

title.narrative: Tsinjo Soa: Expanding Home Toilet Services in Madagascar

description.narrative: The vast majority of Madagascars 29 million people lack access to safe sanitation. In addition to daily sanitation risks, Madagascars high water table is prone to flooding, which creates prime conditions for fecal-borne diseasessuch as diarrhea, cholera, typhoid, and dysenteryto spread. Loowatt, a United Kingdom-based private company, has developed a waterless flush, container-based sanitation device that is not only hygienic and odor-free, but that also leaves a clean bowl after each flush. With the press of a button, a polymer bag that lines the container is pulled down and sealed after each use, keeping the contents contained. Loowatt SARL, a locally-run servicing company, clears the lined containers for an affordable monthly service fee and converts the waste into energy and fertilizer. This patented, waterless flush technology is less expensive to install and maintain than traditional sanitation options, such as pit latrines and toilets with septic tanks. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, Loowatt will expand its operations and demonstrate the financial viability of its subscription-based service model. Compared with toilets connected to sewers, the Loowatt toilet could improve the lives of more than 100,000 people every day and save up to 50,000 liters of water per household per year.

title.narrative: Testing Improved Biofortified Maize Seeds and Subsidies

description.narrative: Maize is a staple food in many countries and a significant source of calories for hundreds of millions of people globally. However, conventional maize lacks sufficient amounts of essential micronutrients, including several needed in early childhood development. Nearly half the children in Guatemala suffer from chronic malnutrition and stunting, which can cause cognitive impairment, weakened immunity, and increased risk of developing chronic diseases. To improve health outcomes, a Guatemalan organization is working to enhance the quality and adoption of biofortified maize, which is bred to contain higher levels of zinc, iron, and protein. Biofortified maize can improve nutrition and health outcomes but faces barriers to adoption from farmers who traditionally use conventional seeds. Additionally, while biofortified maize has been shown to address malnutrition in sub-Saharan African countries, it has yet to be determined whether traditional preparation methods (nixtamalization) widely used in southern Mexico and Central America affect the bodys ability to absorb the micronutrients in biofortified maize. The implementing partner will use independent researchers to conduct two randomized controlled trials: the first to determine whether the body absorbs sufficient levels of zinc and iron from traditionally prepared biofortified maize and the second to assess how changes to a subsidy program would influence farmer adoption of the improved seeds. The implementing partner will use the results of both studies to model the overall impact of biofortified maize on health outcomes in Guatemala, including how it may reduce zinc, iron, and protein deficiencies as more people consume it. The rigorous evidence generated by these studies will provide valuable information on the effectiveness of biofortified maize for improving nutrition and on the cost-effectiveness of such subsidies to combat malnutrition in Guatemala and the region.

PxP is a grant to provide direct and accessible support that addresses the needs, opportunities, and challenges identified by activists, and other civic actors engaged in nonviolent collective action. through this support, PxP will strengthen the agency, resiliency, and efficacy of activists and people-powered social movements that advance human rights, social justice, democracy, and inclusive development. The project will work with these communities to co-create PxP to ultimately elevate locally led approaches and build on existing platforms and networks of support for nonviolent collective action. The grant will be managed by a prime, alongside a consortium of international, regional organizations, who will work to regrant funding to activists, civil society organizations, informal grassroots initiatives, and create offline and online spaces for learning, sharing, and exchange.

title.narrative: One Health Approaches to Mitigate Brucellosis

description.narrative: Brucellosis control strategies must be optimized for the target context. However, there is a dearth of data on the biological, ecological, social, and cultural factors that influence brucellosis spread in sub-saharan africa. There are also gaps in understanding the leverage points to influence individuals, communities, and national systems to enact measures to improve the control of disease. The key objective of this activity is to develop quantitative and qualitative tools such as epidemiological models and social and behavior change research to inform the design of evidence- and risk-based control measures. This evidence will also complement future technical innovations such as improved vaccines, diagnostics, and treatments.

title.narrative: Future Climate Resilient Cereals Innovational Lab (CRCIL)

description.narrative: CRCL aims to design, lead, and implement a research program focused on the discovery/identification of novel alleles for traits critical in climate adaptation, validate and transfer to elite lines of rice, wheat, sorghum and millet in FTF countries and adjacent areas with similar farming systems.

The Farmer-to-Farmer (F2F) Program provides technical assistance from U.S. volunteers to farmers, farm groups, agribusinesses and other agriculture sector institutions in developing and transitional countries with the goal of promoting sustainable improvements in food security, agricultural processing, production, financing, and marketing. F2F leverages the expertise of volunteers from U.S. farms, universities, cooperatives, private agribusinesses and nonprofit farm organizations to respond to the local needs of host-country farmers and organizations. The program is aimed at reducing poverty and stimulating sustainable and broad-based economic growth.

USAID and the Natural Climate Solutions Division plan to develop a user-friendly, freely available, on-line tool to calculate Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions and carbon storage associated with Agriculture, Forestry, and Other Land Use (AFOLU). This tool, the updated AFOLU Calculator tool, will build off USAID's current AFOLU calculator tool, which was originally developed for USAID in 2012. The tool will be used to facilitate required reporting through Agency approved portfolio management systems, etc. on standard USAID climate indicators, assist with activity planning, and align with the priorities of the USAID Climate Strategy.

title.narrative: Ending Neglected Diseases through Operational Research (ENDOR)

description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): Funds will support the optimization of NTD control and elimination, coordinated by the Task Force for Global Health, through the following: define and research operational roadblocks that hinder the successful implementation of NTD programs and progress toward control and elimination goals; link and engage researchers, country-level program staff, implementation partners, and the donor community to build and accelerate consensus to answer key operational questions; support operational research to improve mapping strategies; develop tools and strategies to improve mass drug administration coverage and close compliance gaps; reduce existing morbidity; optimize and develop new diagnostics; and build capacity by awarding small grants to young African researchers working in NTDs. These activities aim to remove barriers and improve program efficiencies to safeguard NTD investments...ENDOR supports a research agenda on the nascent field of female genital schistosomiasis with an emphasis on diagnosis, healthcare worker clinical competencies, and linkage to the health system.
